data.title: Rac1 regulates the activity of mTORC1 and mTORC2 and controls cellular size
data.authors: Saci A; Carpenter CL et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Rac1 binds and regulates both mTORC1 and mTORC2, controlling their localization and cell growth.
data.abstract_excerpt: Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) is a serine/threonine kinase that exists in two separate complexes, mTORC1 and mTORC2, that function to control cell size and growth in response to growth factors, nutrients, and cellular energy levels. Low molecular weight GTP-binding proteins of the Rheb and Rag families are key regulators of the mTORC1 complex, but regulation of mTORC2 is poorly understood. Here, we report that Rac1, a member of the Rho family of GTPases, is a critical regulator of both mTORC1 and mTORC2 in response to growth-factor stimulation.

extracted_findings.effect: Rac1 is a critical regulator of both mTORC1 and mTORC2, controlling cell size
